summary: Full RE of the UX surface of state 0x11 (wpcvw_view_main_loop @ wpcvw 0x67f6) — the interactive character-sheet shown to the player. Documents: (1) the three windows created on entry (right-side stats panel + full-screen main-panel + bottom party-row), (2) the 11-option main menu CAST/EQUIP/etc with its labels actually being EQUIP/SPELL/TRADE/ASSAY/SWAG/MERGE/USE/DROP/SKILL/EDIT/REVIEW (per indexed msg table id 301-311), (3) the full dispatch table at file 0x6b8a (wpcvw runtime delta = 0x4564, same as wpcmk) mapping picker index → handler offset, (4) the context-sensitive enable mask for *0x4fce==4 (camp) vs *0x4fce==0xd (in-combat) vs default (dungeon), (5) the per-character disables (gold==0+inv_empty=>TRADE off, inv_count==0=>ASSAY/USE/DROP off, inv_count<2=>MERGE off, !is_active=>SPELL/USE off), (6) the EDIT submenu (RENAME/CHANGE PORTRAIT/CHANGE PROFESSION/REPLACE/EX) at 0x671f with msg-base 650, (7) name-edit at 0x6674 calling ui_text_input_editor (max 7 chars), (8) PORTRAIT-change flow at 0x63bc (was misnamed 'identify_shop_or_temple' in prior pass), (9) state 0x16 (bulk levelup) handler at 0xb4ac that calls wpcvw_per_character_levelup_loop for every party member — which IS partially interactive (level_pick_new_spells_loop prompts YES/NO per spell). **Major correction to prior findings**: case-5 cursed-item-lockout in wpcvw-naming-pass was wrong — the cursed flag check (0x40|0x02|0x01) is actually in case **7 (DROP)**, not case 5 (which is MERGE). The DROP handler calls inventory_equip_or_unequip (0x17f7) AFTER the cursed-check passes; that misnaming suggests the function is a unequip-then-drop wrapper, NOT a pure equip toggle. Also: prior finding said DROP doesn't check cursed bits — actually the OPPOSITE is true (DROP does check 0x01|0x02|0x40).
method: (a) ndisasm -b 16 wpcvw.ovr to read raw bytes 0x6800-0x6bd0 for view-main-loop control flow + dispatch; (b) PyGhidra DecompInterface on wpcvw_view_main_loop (file 0x67f6), wpcvw_edit_submenu (0x671f), wpcvw_edit_name (0x6674), wpcvw_per_character_levelup_loop (0xb362), wpcvw_apply_levelup (0xb220), state-0x16 handler at 0xb4ac, ui_menu_picker_grid (0x6c), ui_pick_inventory_item (0x1a48), ui_render_full_character_sheet (0x4e94), ui_render_character_stats_panel (0xf47); (c) Python search of wpcvw.ovr for the jump table by trying all 16-bit deltas — found wpcvw runtime delta = 0x4564 (SAME as wpcmk), table at file 0x6b8a, order = picker_index → handler_file_offset; (d) cross-reference with indexedMessages in extracted/messages/msg.json — msg ids 301-311 give EQUIP/SPELL/TRADE/ASSAY/SWAG/MERGE/USE/DROP/SKILL/EDIT/REVIEW; msg 650-654 give EDIT submenu RENAME/CHANGE PORTRAIT/CHANGE PROFESSION/REPLACE/EX; msg 1112-1128 give portrait-change + name-edit prompts; (e) prior finding cross-references: wbase-party-pickers-and-dismiss.json defines state-0x11 entry mechanics (already implemented); wpcvw-naming-pass.json defines 90 function names — this pass uses ~30 of them and corrects 1.

wpcvw_runtime_delta_discovery.claim: wpcvw.ovr runtime delta is 0x4564 (identical to wpcmk.ovr's delta documented in CLAUDE.md). Confirmed by finding the 11-entry jump table at file 0x6b8a containing handler offsets {0x6a17, 0x6a29, 0x6a3e, 0x6a50, 0x6b3d, 0x6b1a, 0x6ae8, 0x6a86, 0x6b4e, 0x6b2c, 0x6b5c} each offset by +0x4564 to their CS:runtime values referenced by the `jmp word [cs:bx+0xb0ee]` dispatch at file 0x6ba8. The table values are u16 little-endian at file offsets 0x6b8a, 0x6b8c, 0x6b8e, ... 0x6b9e.
wpcvw_runtime_delta_discovery.verification: python3 -c 'import struct; d=open("original/wpcvw.ovr","rb").read(); ws=[struct.unpack("<H",d[0x6b8a+2*i:0x6b8a+2*i+2])[0] for i in range(11)]; assert all(0x6a00 <= ((w-0x4564)&0xffff) <= 0x6c00 for w in ws)'
wpcvw_runtime_delta_discovery.implication_for_findings_in_this_file: All CS-disp16 references inside wpcvw asm (e.g. jump tables, condition-icon table at cs:0x532, class-dispatch tables at cs:-NNNN) need (CS_offset - 0x4564) to get file offset. Update CLAUDE.md overlay-delta table when this is promoted.

findings.claim: wpcvw_view_main_loop @ wpcvw 0x67f6 creates EXACTLY THREE windows on entry, in this order: (1) **STATS-PANEL** (stored at global `*0x5752`): x=20, y=4, w=20, h=16, attr=0x1a — the right-side stats panel where ui_render_character_stats_panel writes portrait+name+race+sex+AC+HP/SP+level+class+armor-class+gold; (2) **MAIN-PANEL** (local var `[bp-4]` aka local_4): x=0, y=0, w=40, h=20, attr=0x14 — the full-screen foreground window that holds the inventory grid + ACTION menu picker; this is also the picker's host window; (3) **PARTY-ROW** (local var `[bp-2]` aka local_6): x=0, y=20, w=40, h=4, attr=0x0f — the bottom mini-portrait strip (party row). Window 2 (MAIN-PANEL) is created AFTER the STATS-PANEL but they're spatially disjoint (rows 0-19 vs the stats-panel inside rows 4-19 columns 20-39); the stats-panel sits inside the full-screen window's right half. After all three are created, the engine unfocuses *0x4fb2 (persistent menu/banner) and clears global *0x57fc (some redraw-suppress flag).

evidence.details: ndisasm of file 0x6814-0x689d shows three sequential ui_window_create calls (target 0xbbb6 = wroot's ui_window_create thunk). Args (cdecl, pushed right-to-left): Window 1 push sequence at 0x6811-0x682d → (x=0x14, y=4, w=0x14, h=0x10, attr=0x1a, chrome=0xffff, flags=0, refresh=0); return stored at `mov [0x5752], ax` (0x6834). Window 2 push sequence at 0x685d-0x6873 → (x=0, y=0, w=0x28, h=0x14, attr=0x14, chrome=0xffff, 0, 0); stored at `mov [bp-2], ax` (0x687a). Window 3 push sequence at 0x687d-0x6899 → (x=0, y=0x14, w=0x28, h=4, attr=0xf, chrome=0xffff, 0, 0); stored at `mov [bp-4], ax` (Ghidra local_6). ui_window_create signature from docs/re/wbase-main-menu.md: (x, y, w, h, attr, chrome, flags, refresh).

findings.supersedes: wpcvw-view-main-window-geometry in wbase-party-pickers-and-dismiss.json (the prior finding had window-2/3 mixed up and noted uncertainty about the h=0x28 value — it was actually the second window's w=0x28 with h=0x14, not h=0x28).

findings.claim: Per loop iteration, after window setup, the view calls `ui_render_full_character_sheet(slot, mainPanel, statsPanel)` at wpcvw 0x4e94. This is a 9-line composite renderer that: (1) clears the STATS-PANEL with fill=0x20 attr=3, (2) clears the MAIN-PANEL with fill=0x20 attr=3, (3) refreshes via func_0x0000ebb4, (4) calls ui_draw_character_sheet_borders (file 0xea0? prior pass — TODO confirm), (5) calls ui_render_character_stats_panel @ wpcvw 0xf47 (the 1.8KB stats renderer with portrait + name + race + AC + HP/SP), (6) calls ui_render_inventory_panel @ wpcvw 0x6c81 (renders the inventory grid + 6 attribute values + AC), (7) calls func_0x0000ec6d on stats panel (unfocus / commit), (8) calls func_0x0000e4ff (final composite/blit).

evidence.details: Ghidra decompile of ui_render_full_character_sheet shows exactly those 8 function calls in order. The 5th call uses 0xf47 = ui_render_character_stats_panel (per wpcvw-naming-pass.json fn-stats-render), the 6th uses 0x6c81 = ui_render_inventory_panel (per fn-inventory-render).

findings.claim: The main action menu has exactly **11 options** (indices 0-10) plus an implicit EXIT (index 11). The labels come from the indexed message table at id 301-311 (msg.json `indexedMessages` keyed by `id`): **0=EQUIP, 1=SPELL, 2=TRADE, 3=ASSAY, 4=SWAG, 5=MERGE, 6=USE, 7=DROP, 8=SKILL, 9=EDIT, 10=REVIEW**, and the picker treats result==11 as EXIT (handled at 0x6bad: `cmp ax, 0xb / jnc 0x6bad / cmp [bp-0x6], 0xb / jz exit_cleanup`). The picker is `ui_menu_picker_grid` (file 0x6c) called with `(window=local_4, msg_base=0x12d=301, mask_ptr=[bp-0x24], x_base=2, y_base=1, x_step=6, cols=2, attr=5, init_cursor=count_of_enabled)`. Layout: 2 cols × 6 rows (so up to 12 cells visible, 11 used). Cursor moves with arrow keys (1=UP, 2=LEFT, 3=DOWN, 4=RIGHT), Enter (key code 5) commits. Mouse click sets cursor and commits via `*0x4fc4 == 1`.

evidence.details: ndisasm at 0x69dd: push 0xb (count); lea [bp-0x24]; push; call menu_count_enabled_entries (0x1681); add sp,4; push ax (init_cursor=enabled count). Then push 5 (attr); push 2 (cols); push 6 (x_step); push 1 (y_base); push 2 (x_base); push lea [bp-0x24] (mask); push 0x12d (msg_base); push [bp-4] (window=local_4 — main-panel from window-layout finding); call ui_menu_picker_grid; add sp, 0x12. Picker labels resolved via `python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("extracted/messages/msg.json")); by_id={m["id"]:m for m in d["indexedMessages"]}; [print(k, by_id.get(k,{}).get("decodedText")) for k in range(0x12d, 0x139)]'` → EQUIP/SPELL/TRADE/ASSAY/SWAG/MERGE/USE/DROP/SKILL/EDIT/REVIEW/EXIT.

findings.claim: The picker-result → action-handler jump table lives at **file 0x6b8a** in wpcvw.ovr — 11 little-endian u16 entries totaling 22 bytes. The table is referenced by `jmp word [cs:bx+0xb0ee]` at file 0x6ba8 (with bx = 2*picker_result). Each entry is a CS-runtime address; subtract the wpcvw runtime delta 0x4564 to get the file offset of each handler. Dispatch ORDER (picker_index → handler_file_offset / function): **0 EQUIP → 0x6a17 (call 0x8e35 = wpcvw_unequip_all_and_recompute — likely misnamed, may be EQUIP-from-pool); 1 SPELL → 0x6a29 (call FUN_416d, unnamed in prior pass — likely 'cast spell out of combat'); 2 TRADE → 0x6a3e (call 0x513e = wpcvw_give_to_party_member); 3 ASSAY → 0x6a50 (call ui_pick_inventory_item with msg 0x1c2='ASSAY WHICH ITEM?' then 0x7160 = wpcvw_item_inspect_and_use); 4 SWAG → 0x6b3d (call 0x1db3 = wpcvw_show_pool_inventory — name fits 'SWAG' = pool/share treasure); 5 MERGE → 0x6b1a (call FUN_5826, unnamed — stack-merging for ammo/scrolls/potions); 6 USE → 0x6ae8 (call ui_pick_inventory_item with msg 0x190='USE WHICH ITEM?' then 0x4a5b = wpcvw_item_drop_or_give_dispatch — likely misnamed, is the USE-per-item-type dispatch); 7 DROP → 0x6a86 (call ui_pick_inventory_item with msg 0x192='DROP WHICH ITEM?' then cursed-flag check, then 0x17f7 = inventory_equip_or_unequip); 8 SKILL → 0x6b4e (call 0x4d36, unnamed in prior pass — scans skills[0x451c+0x11..+0x16] for available skills then shows picker); 9 EDIT → 0x6b2c (call 0x671f = wpcvw_edit_submenu); 10 REVIEW → 0x6b5c (call ui_pick_party_member with msg 0x1f4='REVIEW WHO?' then sets *0x43cc to new leader slot, *0x57fc:=0).**

evidence.details: Python search: `for delta in range(0,0x10000): if {h+delta for h in {0x6a17,...}} matches any 22-byte block — delta=0x4564 at file 0x6b8a, order=[0x6a17, 0x6a29, 0x6a3e, 0x6a50, 0x6b3d, 0x6b1a, 0x6ae8, 0x6a86, 0x6b4e, 0x6b2c, 0x6b5c]`. ndisasm at file 0x6ba8: `2E FF A7 EE B0` = `jmp word [cs:bx+0xb0ee]`. CS:0xb0ee + 0x4564 file delta → file 0xb0ee - 0x4564 = ... wait, the displacement 0xb0ee references the runtime CS address of the table. Runtime CS:0xb0ee = file_offset 0x6b8a → delta = 0xb0ee - 0x6b8a = 0x4564. Confirmed.

findings.claim: When state 0x11 is entered from camp / wbase main menu (`*0x4fce == 4` — see wpcvw-view-main-loop-immediate-state-overwrite finding), the engine DISABLES most destructive actions. Asm at file 0x68e9-0x6929: first zero all 11 mask slots, then enable indices **0 (EQUIP), 1 (SPELL), 3 (ASSAY), 4 (SWAG), 8 (SKILL), 10 (REVIEW)**, then also clear `[bp-0x26]` (a separate flag, possibly the EXIT/cancel availability). So the camp view is EQUIP/SPELL/ASSAY/SWAG/SKILL/REVIEW/EXIT — 7 enabled options. **Cross-check needed** — this means EDIT (rename/portrait/class) is NOT available from camp's REVIEW MEMBER; that's surprising because users typically expect those from a 'review' screen. The user's lived recollection should be authoritative here.

evidence.details: asm at 0x68e9-0x6929: `cmp word [0x4fce], 4 / jnz +0x3b / for si=0..0xa: [bp-0x24 + 2*si] := 0` (clear all 11 mask slots); then `[bp-0x24]:=1 (mask[0]=EQUIP); [bp-0x1e]:=1 (mask[3]=ASSAY); [bp-0x14]:=1 (mask[8]=SKILL); [bp-0x10]:=1 (mask[10]=REVIEW); [bp-0x22]:=1 (mask[1]=SPELL); [bp-0x1c]:=1 (mask[4]=SWAG); [bp-0x26]:=0`. Mask offsets verified by the init loop at 0x68d3 which writes `[bp-0x24 + 2*si] := 1` for si=0..0xa (11 entries), so [bp-0x24]=idx0..[bp-0x10]=idx10.

open_followups: Q: Does the original wiz6 game UI actually hide TRADE/USE/DROP/MERGE/EDIT options when viewing a character from camp's REVIEW MEMBER? User lived recollection > asm reading here, but the asm is unambiguous so I expect yes.

findings.claim: When state 0x11 is entered with `*0x4fce == 0xd` (combat-related state — possibly post-combat treasure or combat-pause), the mask is set differently: enabled = **0 (EQUIP), 1 (SPELL), 3 (ASSAY), 4 (SWAG), 7 (DROP), 8 (SKILL)**. This is a 6-action set, REPLACING REVIEW with DROP compared to the camp set. The TRADE/USE/MERGE/EDIT options remain disabled. EDIT being disabled in combat makes sense (no time to rename or change class mid-fight); the addition of DROP is curious — possibly for unloading inventory weight during combat? **Mark as medium-confidence — the *0x4fce==0xd context is the WMEXE state (combat action resolution) per CLAUDE.md state machine, but it's not obvious when the player would enter VIEW PC during combat. May actually be the post-combat TREASURE flow (state 0xf) reading *0x4fce instead.**

evidence.details: asm at 0x692b-0x696b: `cmp word [0x4fce], 0xd / jnz +0x39 / for si=0..0xa: [bp-0x24 + 2*si] := 0 / [bp-0x24]:=1 (EQUIP); [bp-0x16]:=1 (DROP); [bp-0x1e]:=1 (ASSAY); [bp-0x14]:=1 (SKILL); [bp-0x22]:=1 (SPELL); [bp-0x1c]:=1 (SWAG); [bp-0x26]:=0`.

open_followups: Q: Under what conditions does *0x4fce == 0xd at WPCVW entry? State 0xd is wmexe (combat action resolution); does that overlay invoke wpcvw? Or does *0x4fce hold a different sentinel for 'just-finished-combat' that happens to equal 0xd?

findings.claim: Default branch (*0x4fce neither 4 nor 0xd, typically 5 = wmaze/dungeon): ALL 11 actions enabled before per-character disables apply. This is the in-dungeon VIEW PC mode invoked via wmaze hotkey — the full set of actions is available. The per-character disable rules then apply: (i) party_size < 2 (`*0x43ce < 2`) disables mask[2]=TRADE and mask[10]=REVIEW; (ii) `slot+0x4594 == 0` (inventory count zero) disables mask[3]=ASSAY, mask[6]=USE, mask[7]=DROP; (iii) `slot+0x4594 < 2` (need 2+ items to merge) disables mask[5]=MERGE; (iv) gold == 0 AND inventory empty disables mask[2]=TRADE (redundant with i if alone, but covers party_size>=2 case where char has nothing to trade); (v) `wpcvw_is_character_active(slot) == 0` (sex==0 OR dead OR paralyzed/stone) disables mask[1]=SPELL, mask[6]=USE.

evidence.details: asm at 0x68ce-0x69d4: `[bp-0x26]:=1` then init loop sets all 11 mask slots to 1; then 4fce==4 branch / 4fce==0xd branch (above) / fallthrough (default). Then disable checks: 0x696b cmp [0x43ce], 2 / jnl skip / [bp-0x10]:=0 (REVIEW) / [bp-0x20]:=0 (TRADE); 0x697c cmp byte [bx+0x4594], 0 / jnz / [bp-0x1e]:=0 (ASSAY), [bp-0x16]:=0 (DROP), [bp-0x18]:=0 (USE); 0x699a cmp byte [bx+0x4594], 2 / jnc / [bp-0x1a]:=0 (MERGE); 0x69a6 gold-hi & gold-lo & inv-count == 0 / [bp-0x20]:=0 (TRADE); 0x69c0 call wpcvw_is_character_active (0x5b11) / test ax / jnz / [bp-0x22]:=0 (SPELL), [bp-0x18]:=0 (USE).

findings.claim: The view main loop is a top-of-function `while (true)` that: (1) renders the full character sheet via ui_render_full_character_sheet (which redraws portrait+stats+inventory each cycle, allowing the picker to overlay menu labels on the main panel), (2) re-evaluates the 11-entry enable mask each iteration (so mask reflects current gold/inv-count/conditions even after actions modify them), (3) calls ui_menu_picker_grid which blocks on input, (4) if picker returns 0..10, jumps into per-action handler via the cs:0xb0ee jump table; each handler returns and falls through to `jmp 0x6bad` which loops back to render (UNLESS picker returned 0xb=EXIT, in which case it calls wpcvw_state_0x11_exit_cleanup @ 0x5b4a and returns). The handlers are responsible for clearing/redrawing the main panel themselves if they show sub-windows; the outer loop unconditionally re-renders on the next iteration so transient sub-UIs don't need to clean up perfectly.

evidence.details: Loop body at 0x68bf: push slot, [bp-2] (mainPanel), [bp-4] (statsPanel); call ui_render_full_character_sheet (0x4e94). 0x68ce mask init. 0x68e9, 0x692b, default — context-mask branches. 0x696b-0x69d4 per-character disables. 0x69d5 call func_0x0000e2a8 (some redraw helper). 0x69dd-0x6a0b picker call. 0x6a11 store result. 0x6a14 jmp 0x6ba0 → dispatch table. After each case-handler: jmp 0x6bad → cmp [bp-0x6], 0xb / jz 0x6bb6 (exit-cleanup) / jmp 0x68bf (loop back to render).

findings.claim: EXIT path: when picker returns 0xb (cancel/Enter on the EXIT entry — picker treats 11 as 'option 11', which the dispatch SKIPS via `cmp ax, 0xb / jnc 0x6bad / cmp [bp-0x6], 0xb / jz 0x6bb6`), code at file 0x6bb6 calls: (1) `func_0x0000bd6e(*0x5752, 0)` — destroy the STATS-PANEL (window 1); (2) push [bp-2] (mainPanel local_4), [bp-4] (partyRow local_6); call wpcvw_state_0x11_exit_cleanup @ 0x5b4a. The cleanup function (already documented in wbase-party-pickers-and-dismiss.json#wpcvw-exit-cleanup-cleanup-only) destroys those two remaining windows and refocuses/redraws *0x4fb2 based on what state we're returning to. Critically: *0x363a was ALREADY overwritten from *0x4fce at the FIRST instruction of view_main_loop, so the EXIT path does NOT need to set a return state — the dispatcher just returns to the outer state-machine, which immediately picks up the pre-armed state.

evidence.details: ndisasm at 0x6bb6-0x6bd4: push 0; push [0x5752]; call ui_window_destroy (0xbd6e thunk); add sp,4; push [bp-2]; push [bp-4]; call wpcvw_state_0x11_exit_cleanup (0x5b4a); add sp,4; pop si; mov sp,bp; pop bp; ret. Cross-reference: wbase-party-pickers-and-dismiss.json finding wpcvw-exit-cleanup-cleanup-only documents the cleanup function's body.

findings.claim: The EDIT submenu (case 9 from main menu, calls wpcvw_edit_submenu @ 0x671f) is a 5-option grid menu: **0=RENAME CHARACTER (msg 650), 1=CHANGE PORTRAIT (msg 651), 2=CHANGE PROFESSION (msg 652), 3=REPLACE CHARACTER (msg 653) — FORCE-DISABLED at runtime, 4=EX (EXIT — msg 654 'EX')**. The submenu loops just like the main menu — picker returns option, handler is called, picker is shown again — until option 4 is picked. The mask at the start of each iteration sets [0..4]=1 then forces [3]:=0 (the REPLACE CHARACTER option is always disabled — possibly only available from wpcmk). The picker uses (window=mainPanel_param_2, msg_base=0x28a=650, mask, x_base=2, y_base=1, x_step=0x12, cols=2, attr=5).

evidence.details: Ghidra decompile: `local_1a[0..4] := 1; local_1a[3] := 0; local_10 := 0xffff; uVar1 = menu_count_enabled(local_1a, 4); local_6 = ui_menu_picker_grid(param_2, 0x28a, local_1a, 2, 1, 0x12, 2, 5, uVar1); if (local_6 == 0) wpcvw_edit_name(param_2, param_3); else if (local_6 == 1) wpcvw_identify_shop_or_temple(param_2, param_3); else if (local_6 == 2) wpcvw_class_change_execute(param_1, param_2, param_3); ui_render_full_character_sheet(param_1, param_2, param_3); while (local_6 != 4);`. Note count is 4 (not 5) because the picker iterates the mask until it sees the 0xffff terminator at local_1a[5] OR reaches count=4. msg lookup via indexedMessages[650..654] = RENAME CHARACTER / CHANGE PORTRAIT / CHANGE PROFESSION / REPLACE CHARACTER / EX.

findings.claim: RENAME flow (EDIT submenu option 0): wpcvw_edit_name @ wpcvw 0x6674. Clears+borders the main-panel window. Shows msg 0x468 ('NEW NAME >') at position (1, 1). Calls `ui_text_input_editor` @ wpcvw 0x4ef5 with a 7-char (`uStack_a = 7`) max-length buffer, cursor at (5, 7) inside the window. If the user commits a non-empty name (`local_c[0] != 0`), calls func_0x0000f3aa (probably strcpy thunk) to copy the buffer to `slot * 0x1b0 + 0x43e8` (the character-record name field — confirmed by wpcvw-naming-pass bss_layout: name at +0x0). If the user cancels (empty), name is unchanged.

evidence.details: Ghidra decompile: window clear+border (func_0x0000ed5a, func_0x0000e4ff), cursor set (func_0x0000bda7(window, 1, 1)), put msg 0x468 (func_0x0000c2db(0x468, window)), then ui_text_input_editor(...) with uStack_a=7 (max chars), uStack_8=5 (cursor_x), pppuStack_6=0 (initial cursor pos in buf), local_c=stack buffer. After: if first byte of local_c != 0, strcpy(slot*0x1b0+0x43e8, local_c). Cross-ref: msg lookup in extracted/messages/msg.json indexedMessages by id 0x468 → 'NEW NAME >'.

findings.claim: CHANGE PORTRAIT flow (EDIT submenu option 1): wpcvw_identify_shop_or_temple @ wpcvw 0x63bc — **THE FUNCTION NAME IN PRIOR PASS IS WRONG**. This is the portrait-change screen, NOT identify/shop/temple. It creates a new window with the same geometry as the stats-panel (x=0x14, y=4, w=0x14, h=0x10, attr=0x1e), draws borders, shows msg 0x458 (' TO REVIEW PORTRAITS') at row 1 and msg 0x459 ('PRESS  TO SELECT') at row 2, then enters a loop that: (1) loads a portrait via `portrait_load_from_disk` @ 0x6229 whenever the on-disk portrait index differs from the displayed one (compares `slot+0x4584` vs the per-overlay last-shown global), (2) calls `ui_render_identify_or_shop_row` @ 0x6347 to draw the portrait at (6, 8), (3) polls input via input_poll_key_or_mouse_with_blink. The portrait index advances on arrow keys (need to RE the input handler at later asm — left/right cycle through the portraits pool). Commits the chosen portrait by updating slot+0x4584. **Subagent caution**: function 0x6347 named `ui_render_identify_or_shop_row` is also misnamed — it's the portrait-row renderer.

findings.claim: The picker's initial cursor position on first entry is set to `enabled_count` (the COUNT of enabled options, NOT 0 or the EXIT entry). Asm at 0x69e5: `call menu_count_enabled_entries; push ax` — the count IS the cursor init. This means: if 7 options are enabled, the cursor starts AT position 7 (which would be the 7th enabled option). The first entry to the picker has `[bp-4] := 0` (set at function entry — wait, the param_1 cursor arg comes from `[bp-4]`, but local_4 is the second window, not a cursor...). **Need re-check** — the picker's last-pushed arg is `[bp-4]`. But [bp-4] is local_4 (the main-panel window handle). So `param_9` = window handle? No — the picker signature has param_9 as cursor and param_1 as window. The LAST pushed = param_1 (window). So the window arg IS [bp-4] = mainPanel. The 9th pushed arg (first push, param_9) is `ax` from menu_count_enabled. So **the initial cursor is set to enabled_count** — pointing past the last enabled entry — which the picker code then clamps internally. **Or** it's intentionally placed on EXIT (because the count-of-enabled-among-11 entries is typically 11 when all enabled or 7 when from camp, both of which point at EXIT if EXIT is the 12th entry). TODO confirm against picker internals.

evidence.details: ndisasm at 0x69dd-0x6a0b: count=0xb pushed; lea [bp-0x24] pushed; call menu_count_enabled (returns count of 1's in the 11-entry mask); add sp,4 (clean count args); push ax (use the count as cursor init). This is the LAST push before the cursor arg... wait, picker args are 9, this is one of them. Re-reading: 9 pushes after 0x69e5. Push ax (count) at 0x69eb is arg 8 = param_8 = attr? No: 0x69eb push ax = param_9 cursor (first push). Then 5 (attr), 2 (cols), 6 (xstep), 1 (y), 2 (x), lea [bp-0x24] (mask), 0x12d (msg), [bp-4] (window). So cursor = enabled_count. UX impact: cursor starts on the LAST enabled option (because count - 1 would be the last index, but count itself points one past — picker likely clamps via the wrap-around logic).

implementation_blocking_facts_top_5: 1. **Three windows** are created on view entry: STATS-PANEL (right half x=20,y=4,w=20,h=16,attr=0x1a) stored at GLOBAL *0x5752; MAIN-PANEL (full-screen x=0,y=0,w=40,h=20,attr=0x14) as local; PARTY-ROW (bottom x=0,y=20,w=40,h=4,attr=0x0f) as local. The picker is hosted in the MAIN-PANEL window.
2. **11-option menu** labels are EQUIP/SPELL/TRADE/ASSAY/SWAG/MERGE/USE/DROP/SKILL/EDIT/REVIEW (msg ids 301-311, indexed); plus EXIT (option 12, msg 312) as implicit cancel.

3. **Context-sensitive enable mask**: when entered from camp (*0x4fce==4), only EQUIP/SPELL/ASSAY/SWAG/SKILL/REVIEW are enabled (read-only-ish view). From dungeon (*0x4fce==5 / default), ALL 11 enabled subject to per-character disables (gold/inv/active checks). Combat-related (*0x4fce==0xd): EQUIP/SPELL/ASSAY/SWAG/DROP/SKILL.

4. **EDIT submenu** has 5 entries (msg 650-654: RENAME/CHANGE PORTRAIT/CHANGE PROFESSION/REPLACE/EX); REPLACE is ALWAYS force-disabled. RENAME calls ui_text_input_editor with max-len 7. CHANGE PORTRAIT cycles through portrait pool with left/right arrows. CHANGE PROFESSION applies the class-change tax (level-reset + XP-wipe + saved-old-level cap).

5. **EXIT mechanism**: the view's first statement is `*0x363a := *0x4fce` (pre-arm next state). EXIT just calls cleanup (destroy 3 windows + refocus persistent banner). The dispatcher returns to whatever state is now in *0x363a (4 from camp, 5 from dungeon, etc.). REVIEW WHO option does NOT exit — it changes the viewed character in place.
